metadata.source: Public false positive knowledge, bug bounty experience
metadata.provenance: Synthesized from public knowledge of common false positives

indicators: Payload reflected but not in executable context (e.g., inside <title> without breaking out)
false_positives.verification: Check if payload actually executes, check context, check CSP

indicators: Input validation rejecting quote but not SQLi
Error from different layer (e.g., app error not DB error)
false_positives.verification: Check if error is genuine SQL error, try boolean/time/union to confirm, not just error

indicators: Endpoint returns 403 for other IDs (proper authz)
Data returned is public, not private
ID is random UUID and not guessable, returns 404 not 403 but still not IDOR
false_positives.verification: Check if data is actually private, check if authz check exists, try with two accounts

indicators: URL validation via allow list, blocks private IPs
Response does not contain internal data, just generic
Out-of-band detection without approval, not valid
false_positives.verification: Check if internal data returned, check if allow list blocks, reproduce with internal URL

indicators: Redirect via allow list, blocks external
Redirect requires user interaction and is expected (e.g., login redirect)
false_positives.verification: Check if external redirect allowed, check if allow list

defensive_validation: Review findings for false positives: check alternative explanations, config, WAF, etc. Validate defensively: is finding actually exploitable, or is there mitigation? Identify false positive patterns. Provide alternative explanations.
